source.title: Tasks, stability, architecture, and compute: Training more effective learned optimizers, and using them to train themselves
source.authors: Luke Metz; Niru Maheswaranathan; C. Freeman; B. Poole; Jascha Narain Sohl-Dickstein

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent cutoff or garbling that prevents reading the relevant sections.
record.tranche_reason: Compares held-out performance for Adam and momentum on a ResNet task, a different experimental setup from the optimizer comparisons described in V4. It does not test the other mapped versions.
record.gate_note: The paper's width and batch-size sweeps evaluate a learned optimizer's task generalization; the text does not report those sweeps as tests of the mapped network-generalization claims. Results cited from prior work are not extracted.
record.test_reason: Figure 6 directly compares training and held-out loss for learning-rate-tuned Adam and momentum SGD on two image-classification tasks, bearing on V4. However, the supplied text does not establish which baseline generalizes better, and the plotted curves cannot be recovered from the text extraction.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the ResNet subsection but omits the CIFAR-10 late-overfitting qualification and the paper's broader conclusion: training on diverse tasks at greater scale produces learned optimizers competitive with modestly tuned hand-designed methods, with some transfer to unfamiliar tasks, including training themselves. Transfer remains limited, and self-training deteriorates beyond 10,000 outer iterations.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a learned optimizer and learning-rate-tuned Adam and Momentum to train ResNets; this is not the mapped optimizer-comparison recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance differs by task: the learned optimizer is described as similar to the baselines on CIFAR-10 and slightly worse on resized ImageNet.

fits_no_version.finding: The learned optimizer transfers to unseen tasks and some widths and batch sizes, but can diverge far outside its training distribution.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learned optimizers can generalize across optimization tasks and selected task hyperparameters.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR-10, the learned optimizer performs similarly to the baselines and avoids their late-training overfitting; on resized ImageNet it performs slightly worse.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A learned optimizer trained on validation loss can provide automatic regularization and transfer to ResNet training.

record.code_released: not stated; the authors say they are unable to release a fully running open source implementation due to internal tools.
record.problems: The text gives qualitative descriptions of the ResNet comparison but no extracted numerical train-test gaps or uncertainty for that comparison. Baselines are limited to learning-rate tuning; the authors note that specialized schedules and data augmentation can perform better.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Figure-only curve values were not reconstructed.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out accuracy under the same architecture and training recipe.
Held-out error beyond the width required for zero training error, with training to convergence. Figure 5 reports test loss averaged over 10,000 steps without locating interpolation.
Controlled comparisons of convolutional and fully connected image classifiers, including locality and initialization effects.
Language benchmarks, broader tuning of Adam versus SGD, recovery through decoupled weight decay, and switching from Adam to SGD. The ResNet comparison tunes only learning rates.
Large-batch penalties under matched epoch budgets and their recovery through recipe changes. Figure 5 holds training steps fixed, so changing batch size changes examples processed.
Controlled dropout effects, training-set-size interactions, excessive dropout, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with training–test gaps.
Retraining after removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

missing.what: The separate Adam-versus-momentum comparison on the 35-layer ResNet trained on 64×64 ImageNet is not represented by a row. Add the condition and mark its direction cannot_determine unless the figure becomes readable. The text's slightly-worse statement concerns the learned optimizer, not Adam versus momentum.

record.verdict_notes: No V4 label is justified by the available text: absence of an explicitly reported Adam disadvantage is not evidence that the disadvantage is absent. Figure-only numerical values are declared untranscribed; they have not been inferred. Appendix E's train/test columns refer to task-distribution splits, not the inner models' training–test generalization gaps.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error after widening beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-network generalization.
The Adam-versus-momentum result is on a limited ResNet setup; the paper does not test language models, broader hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, or switching from Adam to SGD.
Whether large batches worsen held-out performance under a fixed epoch budget, or whether recipe changes close that penalty.
Effects of adding dropout, its interaction with training-set size, and removing dropout and weight decay together.
Magnitude-aware sharpness as a predictor of the training-test gap.
Effect of removing memorized training examples on test accuracy.

rows.subject: 14 layer residual network (ResNet V2) trained on CIFAR-10
rows.operation_detail: Trained with learning-rate-tuned Adam; compared with learning-rate-tuned Momentum and the learned optimizer.
rows.measure: Train and test performance during inner-training; authors describe learned-optimizer performance as similar to the baselines.
rows.note: The text does not state whether Adam is better or worse than Momentum on held-out performance; the plotted curves are not numerically transcribed.
rows.check: The recorded value describes the learned optimizer relative to both baselines, not Adam relative to momentum SGD. Similarity to a third optimizer does not establish equality between the baselines or an Adam disadvantage. The measure is training and test loss; no readable pairwise loss difference is supplied. Replace the partial state and withdraw the limits_scope verdict.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: CIFAR-10 ResNet V2, compared with learning-rate-tuned Momentum
reader_labels.reason: The authors report similar performance for the learned optimizer and the baselines, without reporting an Adam disadvantage; see R1.
